_comment: WildMesh3D 'Realistic Animals' main quadruped rig (Boar, Deer, Moose, MountainGoat, Warthog: one bone layout, 105 to 134 bones, most of them face bones and _end leaves) onto Bannerlord's horse_skeleton. Consumed by tools/blender/reskin_animalia_to_horse.py and retarget_animalia_to_horse.py exactly as animalia_to_horse_map.json is; the sources come from tools/blender/export_blend_pack.py. Same method and key meanings as that map. Differences from the Animalia rig: the 'Collarbone' is a real shoulder blade (lateral, withers to shoulder joint), so the front chains keep it; every leg ends in a 'Digit11' hoof bone, so the hooves are joints and need no 'hoof_split'; the spine is Spine1, Spine2, Chest (Chest is the third spine segment); Deer, Moose and MountainGoat add a Neck3, which moves with Neck2 and weights horseneck2. The Moose has only Tail1 and Tail2; the fit skips absent bones. Unlisted groups (ears, eyes, lids, nose, mouth, tongue, beard, ChestL/R) climb to their nearest mapped ancestor: Head or Chest.
_chains_note: Pelvis is in no chain, as in the Animalia map: horsepelvis is a pivot above horsespine1, not a spine segment. The tail is anchored at its root and never stretched. NeckFix1 and NeckFix2 are neck-root helpers parented to Chest; they weight horseneck1 so the neck root follows the neck (check the neck_down bend in the reskin report).

profiles._note: keepneck: every WildMesh neck is far shorter than the horse's (Boar 0.18 m, Deer 0.48 m, Moose 0.38 m from Neck1 to Head), so the default chains stretch it to a horse neck. keepneck moves the neck into place unstretched and unswung, as the Animalia moose profile does; the cost is a horse_head pivot away from the animal's head (the reskin report's joint_residual_after_m names the gap).
